$comment: Execution-loop bookkeeping for automated contributors. Not consumed by the
crate at build or run time; nothing in src/ or tests/ reads this file.
Kept in-tree so a later cycle (or a different session) can see what has
already been tried and, more importantly, what was tried and REJECTED —
the rejected list is the part that stops cycles rediscovering the same

verified_against.note: This crate declares NO [features]; `--all-features` is a no-op here. The authoritative gate is scripts/gate.sh, which spans several workflow files and includes the rustdoc-lint and MSRV passes that reconstructing from ci.yml alone drops.

completed_slots.outcome: PR #315 repaired and merged. Red since 2026-08-02 on one rustdoc error; root cause was structural, not a typo: a commit inserted `struct AbortOnDrop` between `TrackedEntityMap`'s 26-line doc comment and the struct, so AbortOnDrop adopted another type's documentation and `Self::take_dirty` could not resolve. Moved the block back rather than rewriting the link. 5 merge conflicts resolved per-hunk on evidence.

PRs #302 and #305 closed: both descend from root fed9a5e7 while main descends from 9ec08790, so `git merge-tree` reports 'refusing to merge unrelated histories' and GitHub could never have merged them. Both also register FEWER modules than main (167 and 166 vs 169). PR #317 deliberately kept OPEN: it registers 173 modules and carries builtwith/fofa/proxycurl/key_discovery, none of which exist in main.

oathnet door-guard completeness. Copilot's finding on #362 confirmed against source. #363 landed the equivalent code fix in parallel, so #364 narrowed to what #363 shipped without: the pinning test, a fix for a pre-existing test-suite race (reset_budget clears RESPONSE_CACHE, racing the cache tests), and the rate-limit misdiagnosis #363's change made reachable.

cycle_1_slots.instruction: Decide and record the DbWriter unbounded-channel question (OD-1).
cycle_1_slots.status: COMPLETE — DECIDED: keep the channel unbounded, and disclose a pathological backlog. Bounding it would force try_send (drops events, breaking the flush() contract) or an async submit() at a sync engine call site. The queue is also already bounded in practice by DEFAULT_MAX_ENTITIES=2500 and the wall-time watchdog. The real defect was that a storage stall was INVISIBLE, so writer_loop now discloses queue depth past BACKLOG_WARN_EVENTS=1024 with hysteresis at half.

cycle_2_slots.instruction: Make app::update::self_restart honour its documented contract on current_exe() failure.
cycle_2_slots.status: COMPLETE (2597c1f9) — the fn documents 'prints a diagnostic and exits with code 1' but current_exe().expect(...) panicked. current_exe() is a real syscall (/proc/self/exe) and this is the site most likely to see it fail: a self-restart runs right after an update rewrote or unlinked the running binary.

Follows the audit.yml/fuzz.yml precedent (own workflow, advisory, Monday 09:00 UTC + path filter + dispatch). Verified locally: both benches pass, exit 0.

cycle_2_slots.instruction: Fix correlation event lines that render identically for per-entity rules.
cycle_2_slots.status: COMPLETE (8da68560) — FOUND IN REAL SCAN TELEMETRY, not by inspection. A 47-event scan logged `⚡ High cross-source corroboration` nine times byte-identically (12 correlations total). AU-003 correctly emits one Correlation per corroborated entity and each carries a distinguishing `description`; EventKind::log_summary printed only rule_name and discarded it. cli::live had always rendered both, so the event log was the outlier. Two regression tests added.

cycle_3_slots.instruction: Remove the per-event O(n) work the scan views do in the browser during a live scan.
cycle_3_slots.status: COMPLETE (d72041e1) — two hot paths, both behaviour-preserving. (a) scan_info/graph.js resolved correlation-hub corroboration with S.entities.find(...) nested two loops deep: O(correlations x members x entities); a captured 371-entity / 32-correlation scan is millions of string compares per re-layout. Now a uid->entity Map, the pattern the file already used for nodesById. (b) scan_info/log.js re-sorted the type histogram, rewrote its innerHTML, and read box.scrollHeight (forcing synchronous layout) once PER EVENT — ~600 full re-renders and ~600 forced reflows for a 598-event scan. Both are idempotent and only the last is observable, so they coalesce into one animation frame; counting stays synchronous so the breakdown still covers every event.

cycle_3_slots.instruction: Drop the vendored D3 force layout; make the graph extremely basic without losing functionality.
cycle_3_slots.status: COMPLETE (77e73134) — D3 v3 was the last vendored front-end asset (151,725 B) and its continuous force simulation was the most expensive thing the UI did, running over hundreds of nodes on the same device running the scan. Replaced by a deterministic concentric SVG layout computed once in O(nodes), drawn against the DOM with pointer events. Preserved: kind colours, corroboration radius, truncated labels, tooltips, legend, #graph-cap notice, GEXF, Re-layout, Reset view, node drag, canvas pan, pinch/scroll zoom, and every ceiling (GRAPH_MAX_NODES/LINKS, CORR_MAX_SPOKES, star-not-clique). src/web 583,772 -> 439,346 B (-24.7%) and the same bytes leave the binary; VENDOR_FILES is now empty. Deleted a bug class too: the old D3-v3 string-endpoint guard test is obsolete, replaced by one asserting the engine cannot creep back and no per-frame loop runs.

observations.summary: OB-4 RESOLVED, and my earlier smtp_vrfy hypothesis was WRONG. Device debug bundles show `status : Running` — the operator exported them mid-scan, so a log ending at a bare `module >` line is an export boundary, not a hang. Confirmed by counter-example: the 535-event log cuts at `> emailrep` while `smtp_vrfy` COMPLETED in that same run (`smtp_vrfy (1 found)`), and the 598-event log cuts at `> smtp_vrfy`. Different terminal modules, no fixed event cap (598 vs 535) — consistent with export-while-running, not with any one module hanging.
observations.action: closed — do not re-open on log truncation alone

observations.summary: OPEN BUG, not yet fixed: the debug bundle's FULL DOSSIER header prints `modules : 0 run, 0 errored, 0 timed out, 0 skipped, 0 cached, 0 deduped` while the SAME scan's event log records 60 module_done, 9 module_error, 11 module_skipped, 70 module_start (entities 264, status Running). The module counters are dead zeros in the dossier. Cause not yet established — likely the counters are only populated at scan completion, or the dossier reads a default/fresh stats struct. Needs the renderer located (grep for "timed out" / "deduped") and the data source traced before a fix.
observations.action: open — next cycle's highest-value DEBUG candidate

observations.summary: Verified NEGATIVES from the cycle-2 sweep — recorded so later cycles stop re-deriving them. (a) Production `.unwrap()` count is genuinely 0; the 55 production `.expect()` hits are infallible-by-construction (literal Regex::new, aho-corasick over static patterns, tokio runtime / reqwest client init) — the earlier rejection of 'eliminate unwrap/panic/unsafe' is correct as written. (b) All 19 `unsafe` textual hits are CSP header strings ('unsafe-inline') and prose; forbid(unsafe_code) holds. (c) core::classifier does NOT share the IPv4 over-acceptance bug that entity_extractor had: `extract` keeps a dotted-quad only if classify() resolves it to IpAddress, and TargetKind::detect (core/scan/mod.rs:213) gates on `v.parse::<std::net::IpAddr>()`, so 999.1.2.3 and leading-zero forms are already rejected on the engine path. (d) modules/dns_axfr is safe AND already proptested (extract_name_is_total, extract_name_rejects_pointer_loops, build_axfr_query_is_total) — a totality proptest there would be pure duplication.
observations.action: none — negative results, kept to prevent rediscovery

observations.summary: Real-device scan telemetry (two logs, 598 and 47 events, 2026-08-05 and 2026-08-03) shows four module timeouts (nostr 8s, fediverse 8s, signal_radar 14s, device_sensors) and two auth failures that are configuration rather than defects (breach-source HTTP 401 'Invalid or missing API key', github_code_search HTTP 401 'Bad credentials'). crtsh appears as 'capability-quarantined — persistent drift', i.e. the drift system behaving as designed.
observations.action: none this cycle — timeouts are per-module budgets working, not failures; the 401s are unconfigured keys

observations.summary: UNRESOLVED, needs device-side evidence: the 598-event log ends at `04:55:25 module ▶ smtp_vrfy` with no matching ✓/✗ and NO `scan complete` line, whereas the 47-event log terminates cleanly with `✔ scan complete · 10 entities`. Either the scan hung/died in smtp_vrfy (plausible — it dials port 25, which mobile carriers routinely blackhole, so a connect can stall past any read timeout) or the export simply truncated at 598 events. Cannot distinguish from the log alone.
observations.action: open — before treating as a defect, confirm whether the exporter caps event count; if it does not, audit smtp_vrfy's connect timeout specifically (a read timeout does not bound a TCP connect that never completes)

open_defects.summary: DbWriter uses mpsc::unbounded_channel (src/core/engine/writer.rs:39). If event production outpaces sqlite batch writes the queue grows without bound, on a platform whose whole point is a memory-constrained no-root Android device. Exposure INCREASED when #315 raised DEFAULT_SCAN_DEPTH 3->5, since more rounds means more events.
open_defects.status: CLOSED cycle 1 slot 5 — resolved as a disclosure, not a bound. See src/core/engine/writer.rs module docs for why unbounded is correct here and what actually bounds it.
